questions.title: What do you do if your ball rolls back to the same tricky spot after you drop it?
questions.question: You drop your ball to get away from a hard place, but it rolls right back there. What should you do next?

choices.text: Play the ball where it is, or say it's unplayable again
Drop the ball again for free
Move the ball to an easier place with no penalty
Pick up your ball and stop playing the hole

questions.explanation: You must play the ball where it is now, or you can choose to say it's unplayable again but you will get another penalty stroke.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Letting your ball fall from your hand onto the ground following the golf rules.
When your ball is in a spot that's too hard to hit from, so you take a penalty and move the ball.
An extra shot added to your score for breaking a rule or taking relief.

questions.teachingTip: Show kids how to drop a ball the right way, and explain what to do if it rolls to the wrong spot again.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids might think they can keep dropping until the ball lands in a good spot without a penalty.
They may believe they can move the ball wherever they want if they're not happy after a drop.

questions.title: What if your dropped ball ends up back in the same spot?
questions.question: You drop your ball for relief but it rolls back to the same tough place as before. What can you do next?

choices.text: Play the ball as it is, or declare it unplayable again
Move the ball to an easier spot without penalty
Pick up the ball and stop playing the hole

questions.explanation: You must play the ball as it lies, or you may declare it unplayable again and take another penalty stroke.
